versions.changelog:
implementation-self-review 1.0.3

- Added a "Code And Documentation Alignment Gate" to ensure code, tests, and documentation remain synchronized after behavior or contract changes.
- No other functional or logic changes; markdown slightly reorganized for clarity.

implementation-self-review 1.0.2 is a documentation-focused update improving clarity on when and how to use the self-review process.

- Expanded "Purpose" and added a "Use When" section to clarify appropriate contexts for running the skill.
- Introduced a "Required Inputs" section specifying what information is needed for an effective review.
- Refined descriptions and language throughout for conciseness and easier understanding.
- Clarified that the review should avoid file-specific claims when file/diff details are unavailable.
- No code or logic changes; this release reorganizes and clarifies the documentation and guidance only.

This update adds new review gates for error semantics, observability, configuration handling, state/concurrency, and detailed planning convention.

- Introduced Error Semantics, Observability, Configuration & Secret, State/Concurrency, and Test Intent gates for more thorough implementation self-reviews.
- Expanded Iteration Scope Gate with a default documentation directory structure and clarified design history handling.
- Outlined explicit documentation file roles for planning and reviewing features.
- Retained all previous review gates and the step-by-step review workflow.
- No code or functional changes; documentation update only.

Initial release of the implementation-self-review skill.

- Provides a structured self-review process for new or changed implementations, focusing on responsibility boundaries, necessity, file organization, defensive coding, naming clarity, iteration discipline, and rework patterns.
- Includes clear review gates covering placement, necessity, boundaries/defense, naming, same-class scan, iteration scope, and rework stop checks.
- Outlines concise output expectations: list concrete findings, scan for similar issues, propose fixes/simplifications, confirm norms checked, and note verification needs.
- Ensures rework is paused after repeated revisions and steers users toward responsibility boundary realignment when contracts remain unstable.
